nodes_add.name: A. G. Hogg
nodes_add.note: Scottish Presbyterian missionary and philosopher at Madras Christian College; supervised Radhakrishnan's MA thesis (1908)

nodes_add.name: Swami Tapovan Maharaj
nodes_add.note: Born Subrahmanyan Nair in Kerala, 3 December 1889; died 16 January 1957; taught Chinmayananda at Uttarkashi, 1949 onward

nodes_add.name: Swami Pranavananda (Gudivada)
nodes_add.note: Taught Dayananda of Arsha Vidya at Gudivada, Andhra Pradesh, in 1961; credited with his view of the Veda as pramana

nodes_add.name: Swami Tejomayananda
nodes_add.note: Disciple of Chinmayananda; succeeded him as head of Chinmaya Mission

nodes_add.name: Swami Paramarthananda
nodes_add.note: Direct sannyasi disciple of Dayananda of Arsha Vidya; teaches in Chennai

nodes_add.name: Anantanand Rambachan
nodes_add.note: Trinidad-born scholar of Hinduism; studied under Dayananda at Sandeepany from 1973; author of The Limits of Scripture (1994)

nodes_update.name: S. Radhakrishnan
nodes_update.note: Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan; born Tiruttani 5 September 1888; died Madras 17 April 1975; philosopher of intuition and religious experience

nodes_update.name: Swami Chinmayananda
nodes_update.note: Balakrishna Menon; born Ernakulam 8 May 1916; sannyasa from Sivananda 25 February 1949; Chinmaya Mission 1953; died San Diego 3 August 1993

nodes_update.name: Swami Dayananda Saraswati (Arsha Vidya)
nodes_update.note: Natarajan; born Manjakkudi 15 August 1930; sannyasa from Chinmayananda 1962; Arsha Vidya Gurukulam, Saylorsburg, 1986; died Rishikesh 23 September 2015

nodes_update.name: Acharya Prashant
nodes_update.note: Prashant Tripathi; reportedly born Agra 7 March 1978; PrashantAdvait Foundation 2015; Vedanta online, mostly in Hindi

edges_upsert.note: Presented Advaita as 'religion itself' (The Hindu View of Life, 1927)
Radhakrishnan credited Vivekananda with rousing his pride in Hinduism; emphasis on experience
MA supervisor at Madras Christian College; the thesis The Ethics of the Vedanta (1908) answered Christian critics of Vedanta
Studied Gita, Upanishads and Brahma Sutras under him at Uttarkashi, about two years from 1949
Saraswati order of the Dashanami sampradaya via Sivananda
Joined Chinmaya Mission 1952 after hearing him in Madras; sannyasa 1962; taught at Sandeepany from 1963. Replaces the earlier 'lived-with' edge.
Gudivada, 1961; per Rambachan, brought him to the view of the Veda as pramana
Successor as head of Chinmaya Mission (1993); initiation details not checked in this batch
Listed as direct sannyasi disciple (advaita.org.uk; Wikipedia)
Studied under him at Sandeepany, Bombay, about three years from 1973 (Rambachan's obituary)
Self-described Vedanta/Advaita teacher; no guru claimed

places.name: Sandeepany Sadhanalaya, Powai, Mumbai
places.what: Residential Vedanta school opened 1963; VHP founding meeting August 1964; Dayananda taught here

places.name: Sidhbari
places.what: Samadhi shrine at the mission's ashram near Dharamshala

places.name: Rishikesh
places.what: Arsha Vidya Pitham; died here 23 September 2015

glossary.def: A valid means of knowledge, such as perception, inference or scripture.
Offering of knowledge: Chinmayananda's name for a public lecture series on a Vedanta text.
In Advaita, the power or appearance by which the one reality seems to be a world of many things.

issues: figures/chinmayananda.mdx: Wikipedia quotes him in 1993 saying demolishing the Babri Masjid was 'nothing wrong'; I could not see the primary report, so the profile says only that a Times News Service report of 7 January 1993 had him supporting the temple. The checker should locate the original.

figures/chinmayananda.mdx: the quote 'Let us convert Hindus to Hinduism, then everything will be all right' (1964) is sourced only via Wikipedia; needs a primary or scholarly citation (e.g. Katju, Jaffrelot) or removal.

figures/chinmayananda.mdx: Tejomayananda named as successor from general knowledge; not checked in a fetched source this session. Nancy Patchen's biography (1989) cited from memory; verify publisher and year.

figures/dayananda-arsha.mdx: the Anaikatti and Rishikesh centres' founding years, and the year he convened the Hindu Dharma Acharya Sabha (2000 per Wikipedia, 2003 elsewhere), are left out. His Brahma Sutra study in Rishikesh (Wikipedia: three years under Tarananda Giri from 1963) overlaps his 1963 Sandeepany start; left vague.
figures/dayananda-arsha.mdx: Narendra Modi is widely described as his disciple; omitted as not bearing on the teaching and not verified.
figures/dayananda-arsha.mdx: the 1999 context of 'Conversion is Violence' (response to Pope John Paul II's visit and Ecclesia in Asia) was not verified, so it is not stated.

figures/acharya-prashant.mdx: civil service record conflicts (Pioneer: left 'IRPS Services'; Wikipedia: cleared exam but did not pursue). Birth date only from Wikipedia, which is flagged for COI/deletion. No well-documented critical coverage of his teaching was found before the session limit; research was cut short and the Lineage note on influences (e.g. J. Krishnamurti, Kabir) is left out.
figures/acharya-prashant.mdx: the date of the IIT Delhi 'vote merchants' video is not in the Outlook article; described as 'ahead of the Lok Sabha elections'.
figures/radhakrishnan.mdx: the Paul Hacker 'inclusivism' attribution is from general knowledge of the literature, not from a fetched source; check. IEP article author (Michael Hawley) assumed.

parts/neo-vedanta.mdx: consistent with the four profiles. Two small notes: (1) 'Chinmayananda and his student Swami Dayananda' is accurate (sannyasa 1962); (2) the intro's 'Vivekananda and Radhakrishnan rest the claim on mystical experience that anyone can test' versus 'Arsha Vidya teachers hold that the Upanishads are a means of knowledge' matches Rambachan's account; Chinmayananda himself is less clearly on the Arsha Vidya side of that divide than the intro's grouping might suggest.

radhakrishnan: born 5 Sept 1888 Tiruttani; Telugu Niyogi Brahmin; father Sarvepalli Veeraswami -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarvepalli_Radhakrishnan
Lutheran mission school Tirupati 1896; Voorhees College 1900-04; MCC 1904; married 1904; five daughters and a son -> https://iep.utm.edu/radhakri/
A. G. Hogg supervisor; thesis The Ethics of the Vedanta (1908) -> https://iep.utm.edu/radhakri/
quote 'The challenge of Christian critics impelled me to make a study of Hinduism' (MST 19) -> https://iep.utm.edu/radhakri/

Presidency 1909; Mysore 1918; Calcutta George V chair 1921; Andhra VC 1931; Spalding 1936-1952; BHU VC 1939-1948 -> https://iep.utm.edu/radhakri/ ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarvepalli_Radhakrishnan
Hindu View of Life = Upton Lectures 1926, pub. 1927; Idealist View of Life = Hibbert 1929 -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarvepalli_Radhakrishnan ; https://iep.utm.edu/radhakri/

quotes 'a kind of life or experience' (HVL 15); 'The Vedanta is not a religion, but religion itself...' (HVL 23); 'The creeds of religion correspond to theories of science' (IVL 86) -> https://iep.utm.edu/radhakri/
ranked religions by proximity to Advaita; circularity, orientalism critiques; caste defended -> https://iep.utm.edu/radhakri/
Rinehart: 'a theological scheme for subsuming religious difference under the aegis of Vedantic truth' -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarvepalli_Radhakrishnan

chinmayananda: father Kutta Menon judge; Lucknow 1940-43; jailed Punjab 1944; National Herald -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinmayananda_Saraswati

Rishikesh 1947 to write expose; sannyasa 25 Feb 1949 from Sivananda; Tapovan Maharaj Uttarkashi -> https://chinmayamission.com/global/swami-chinmayananda ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinmayananda_Saraswati
Chinmaya Mission formed 8 Aug 1953; global tour 1965; died San Diego 3 Aug 1993 -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinmayananda_Saraswati
VHP 1964 first president; mission stayed out of Ayodhya conflict -> https://www.uni-muenster.de/Religion-und-Politik/en/forschung/projekte/c2-20.html
VHP with S. S. Apte at Sandeepany Aug 1964; 'convert Hindus to Hinduism' quote; BMI chart -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinmayananda_Saraswati
Times News Service 7 Jan 1993, supported temple -> https://www.chinmayaudghosh.in/special-feature/chinmayananda-for-temple
dayananda-arsha: born Natarajan 15 Aug 1930 Manjakkudi; father died when 8; Madras at 17; Air Force; 1952 heard Chinmayananda; secretary; 1961 Pranavananda Gudivada; sannyasa 1962; Sandeepany 1963; courses 1972-79; Piercy 1979; ten courses; four centres; AIM for Seva 2000; Millennium summit 2000; died 23 Sept 2015 Rishikesh; Padma Bhushan 2016 -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dayananda_Saraswati_(Arsha_Vidya)
Saylorsburg gurukulam established 1986; disciples Paramarthananda, Viditatmananda etc. -> https://www.advaita.org.uk/teachers/dayananda.htm

Veda as pramana; quotes 'Ignorance is dispelled only by knowledge...', 'meticulous care in his choice of words', 'the vision of Vedānta in its entirety'; freedom from self-inadequacy; Sandeepany 1973 course; Rambachan from Trinidad -> https://anantrambachan.com/articles/obituary-swami-dayananda-saraswati-1930-2015
conversion 'itself an act of violence'; Bauman Open Theology 2015 -> https://digitalcommons.butler.edu/facsch_papers/1150
